subject: mathematics
question_text: Define the rank of a matrix.

verification.note: Source: Sri Chaitanya, FAST TRACK IPE for Jr. Students — Mathematics-IA (2026-27 edition), book p.34, chapter 5 MATRICES, Very Short Answer question 19. Only the question was taken. The solution, the step order and the mark split are this answer book's own work — see docs/ORIGINALITY_MATHS.md. ⚠ THE MARK SPLIT IS OURS, NOT THE BOOK'S: the Mathematics-IA volume prints no per-step mark allocation on any answer. The 1+1 split rewards the stated definition and a worked example separately, which is how a two-mark definition question is answered in full. Paper position: Maths-1A Section A runs Q1–Q10 at 2 marks each, all compulsory. This is a coaching publication, not a TSBIE document, so the split stays unverified until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. Authoring choice recorded: the card states ONE definition, the minor definition used by the Telangana syllabus, rather than offering the row-echelon count as an alternative in the same breath. recall_prompt: Say the definition of the rank of a matrix, and show it on a small example.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: State the definition
steps.margin_note: First mark. Both parts (i) and (ii) are needed: one non-zero minor of order r, and nothing non-zero above that order. The same fact can be found by row-reducing and counting the non-zero rows, but that is a method, not the definition asked for.
lines: Let A be a non-zero matrix. A positive integer r
is called the rank of A if
(i) A has at least one non-zero minor of order r,
(ii) every minor of order greater than r is zero.
In short, the rank is the order of the largest
non-zero minor of A. It is written Rank A = r.
The rank of a zero matrix is taken as 0.

recall.must_convey: That the rank is the order of the largest non-zero minor: some minor of order r is non-zero and every minor of larger order is zero.
accept: the rank is the order of the largest non zero minor
there is a non zero minor of order r and every minor of bigger order is zero
rank r means some r by r determinant is not zero and all larger ones are
rank ante largest non zero minor yokka order
the rank of the zero matrix is zero

steps.why: Both halves of the definition are needed. Part (i) alone would let any smaller non-zero minor be called the rank, and part (ii) alone is satisfied by the zero matrix, so together they pick out exactly one number.
common_mistakes: Saying the rank is the order of the matrix.
Giving only part (i) and leaving out part (ii).
Saying the rank is the number of rows.
steps.memory_tip: Rank is the size of the LARGEST minor that is not zero, so start big and come down.

steps.label: Give a worked example
steps.margin_note: Second mark. One small matrix worked through shows the definition in use: the 2×2 minor is zero, a 1×1 minor is not, so the rank is 1.
lines: The minor of order 1 given by the entry 1
So the largest non-zero minor has order 1.

recall.must_convey: That in the example the order 2 minor is zero while an order 1 minor is not, so the rank is 1.
accept: the two by two determinant is zero but a single entry is not zero so the rank is one
the largest non zero minor is one by one so rank is one
determinant zero, one by one minor one, rank one
two by two zero, one by one non zero kabatti rank one
rank A equals one for this example

steps.why: The example does the two tests in the order the definition names them, so it shows the definition being used rather than quoted. It also makes the point that a non-zero matrix always has rank at least 1.
common_mistakes: Answering 0 for a matrix that is not the zero matrix.
Checking the 1×1 minor first and stopping there.
steps.memory_tip: A non-zero matrix always has rank at least 1, because some single entry is not zero.
